topic: Pushing things: force and speeding up
why_it_matters: Pushing a shopping cart, a car or a skateboard all follow one rule about how much a shove changes how fast something goes.

concepts.text: Newton's second law: force = mass × acceleration, F = ma
With the same push, more mass means less acceleration (a full cart is harder to get going than an empty one)
Use it: a 10 N push on a 2 kg cart gives a = F ÷ m = 5 m/s²

misconception: Heavier things always speed up more if you push them the same, so a full cart takes off faster than an empty one
root_prerequisite: Speed, push (force) and mass as separate ideas

boss.name: Heavy-Heavy Hippo
boss.backstory: A hippo in a tiny gym headband who carries a sign reading 'HEAVIER = FASTER' and thinks every cart wants to be full.

taunt: I am extremely heavy. Observe how quickly I will now accelerate.
More mass is more speed. It is simply bigger.
I have filled the cart. It will now leave at once.
heal: Splendid. Heft is velocity. I shall have it engraved.
Quite right. The heavy cart wins every race.
hit: This is most irregular. The heavy cart appears to be going nowhere.
I did not authorize an empty cart.
lines.ko: I object to being divided by my own weight.
lines.reformed: I have pushed both carts. The empty one left first. I would like to join you.

cliffhanger: I heard that if you push twice as hard, the speed-up doubles too. Is that the same law? That can't be right… right?

quiz.question: Write the equation that ties force, mass and acceleration together.
quiz.answer: F = m × a (force equals mass times acceleration).

quiz.question: You give an empty cart and a full cart the same push. Which one speeds up more, and why?
quiz.answer: The empty cart. For the same push, more mass means less acceleration.

quiz.question: A 10 N push moves a 2 kg cart. What is its acceleration?
